message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's AITA (Ask if it's a Thing, AITA) for not wanting to be friends with my group anymore. Let me break this down step by step. First, I just finished my freshman year in college and found a good friend group. That's awesome because I've always been shy, so being part of a group means a lot to me. But here's the thing: I'm the only one in a group of eight who isn't in the school's Honors College. People, including my friends, have told me that this doesn't mean they're smarter or harder working, and I've accepted that. So, intellectually, I get that it's not about being better than me. However, the Honors College students have required courses just for them, so they all take classes together without me. When we hang out, everyone talks about their classes, and I feel left out. That's tough because I want to feel included and part of the conversation. It's not just about the classes; it's about the shared experiences that come with being in the same program. Then, I found out that next year, they're all living in the Honors College dorm building together. I can't live there since I'm not in the Honors College, and I already feel left out enough. Now that they'll all live together, it's even more likely they'll end up hanging out without me. They might just run into each other more often because they're all in the same place, and I can't blame them for that. It's natural to spend more time with people who are around you. I tried talking to a couple of them about it, and one person said I have no right to make them feel bad for being happy about living together. That stung because I feel like if they had an ounce of empathy, they'd realize that having seven out of eight people living together is rather unfair. I don't want to start over and find new friends, but I also feel like I deserve friends who will try to include me. So, is it AITA for me to not want to be friends with them anymore? Let me think about this. On one hand, I've built a connection with them, and it's hard to let go. On the other hand, if they can't make an effort to include me, especially when they're all living together, it might be too much for me to handle emotionally. I guess I need to consider whether it's realistic to expect them to make an effort to include me when they're all living together. It's a big change, and proximity plays a huge role in friendships. They might not mean to exclude me, but it's easy to get caught up in the convenience of being around each other all the time. Also, I have to think about my own well-being. If being around them makes me feel left out and unhappy, it's not healthy for me to stay in that situation. It's important to have friends who make me feel valued and included, even if it means finding a new group. In the end, I think it's not wrong to consider not wanting to be friends with them anymore if they can't make an effort to include me. It's about prioritizing my own happiness and mental health. It's tough, but sometimes friendships change, and that's okay.
